summary.text: Long before it is killed, the god Adonalsium makes the worlds of the cosmere.
It works through the four Dawnshards, the primal Commands of creation.
Adonalsium makes the world of Roshar, long before it is Shattered.
On it, Adonalsium makes the first great spren: the Wind, the Stone and the Night.

title.text: An earlier plot against Adonalsium fails

summary.text: Long before the Shattering, someone plots to destroy Adonalsium and fails.
Hoid is born on Yolen, long before he starts wandering the cosmere.

title.text: Hoid comes to hold a Dawnshard

summary.text: Before Adonalsium dies, Hoid comes to hold one of the Dawnshards, almost by accident.
Sixteen people kill Adonalsium, and each takes up one of the sixteen Shards of its power.
Hoid could have taken up a Shard himself, but chooses not to.
The Dawnshards are the weapons that make the killing possible.
It happens on Yolen, the world where humans first appeared.

title.text: The Shards agree to leave one another alone

summary.text: The new Vessels agree not to interfere with one another, though few of them keep to it.
Endowment later counts two Shards settling together as a breach of that pact.

title.text: The Shards scatter across the cosmere

summary.text: The new Vessels carry their Shards away to different worlds; some settle, and others keep wandering.

title.text: Honor and Cultivation settle on Roshar

summary.text: Honor and Cultivation come to Roshar together, and both Invest the world.
Ruin and Preservation settle on Scadrial and, working together, make the world and its people.

title.text: Devotion and Dominion settle on Sel

summary.text: Devotion and Dominion both make their home on Sel.
It breaks the Shards' agreement not to settle together.
The Shard Endowment makes its home on Nalthis.
The Shard Autonomy makes its home on Taldain.
Odium kills the Vessels of Devotion and Dominion and Splinters both Shards.
Odium draws their power into the Cognitive Realm, where it becomes the Dor.

local: more than 7,700 standard years before the True Desolation

title.text: Odium wounds Ambition in the Threnodite system

summary.text: Odium attacks Ambition there, grievously wounding her and scattering parts of her power across the system.

title.text: Odium intervenes in Ashyn’s human conflicts

summary.text: Odium grants powerful Surges to a city-state on Alaswha and backs its conquest of neighboring city-states.

local: c. 8,000 years before the Night of Sorrows

title.text: Honor and Cultivation create intelligent spren

summary.text: They create ten varieties of spren with independent thoughts and passions, including the true spren.

local: c. 8,000 years before the modern Rosharan era

summary.text: After a cataclysm devastates Ashyn, human refugees arrive on Roshar alongside Odium and are received by its singers.

local: c. 7,100 years before the modern Rosharan era

summary.text: Human expansion beyond the land initially granted to the refugees brings humans and singers into open war.

local: c. 7,050 years before the modern Rosharan era

summary.text: Forty-three years into the war, Honor and ten human leaders establish the Oathpact to hold the Fused on Braize.

local: c. 7,000 years before the modern Rosharan era

title.text: A Kerztian ambush devastates the Diem

summary.text: Kerztian warriors attack during a Diem ceremony, leaving Kenton alive among the fallen sand masters.
After finding Kenton alive, Khrissalla’s party accepts his help crossing Dayside, and the two begin cooperating on their investigations.
After returning to the Diem, Kenton takes leadership and challenges the assumption that only the strongest sand masters can lead.

title.text: Kenton preserves the Diem and exposes a conspiracy

summary.text: Kenton defeats Drile in the Diem’s challenge, secures support for the order, and uncovers Elorin’s role in the A’kar’s scheme.
Two weeks later, families return to the Diem, though the A’kar remains intent on regaining influence.
The city is constructed centuries, possibly more than a millennium, before the Reod.

local: centuries to over a millennium before the Reod

summary.text: The first Fjordell Empire collapses about three centuries before the events of Elantris.
An earthquake opens a great chasm in southern Arelon; the landform change disrupts the Aons on which Elantrian magic depends.

title.text: Raoden is taken by the Shaod

summary.text: On the morning of his wedding, the crown prince is transformed and secretly sent to Elantris.
The princess of Teod arrives expecting to marry Raoden, only to be treated as his widow and drawn into Arelon’s court politics.

title.text: Hrathen begins his campaign to convert Arelon

summary.text: The Fjordell gyorn arrives with a short deadline to convert Arelon to Shu-Dereth, escalating the struggle over the kingdom’s future.
Raoden recognizes that the city’s great Aon is incomplete, adds the missing Chasm line, and restores AonDor and the Elantrians.

title.text: Alendi is stopped at the Well

summary.text: Rashek kills Alendi to prevent him from reaching the Well of Ascension.
Rashek takes the power himself, becomes the Lord Ruler, and uses it to alter Scadrial and establish the Final Empire.
Bayala's ruling dynasty collapses in year 480 of the Vorin calendar.

title.text: The War of Loss ends the Hierocracy

summary.text: The War of Loss brings down the Hierocracy and divides Vorinism into devotaries.
A global conflict pits Hanald against a coalition of Nalthian nations after Awakening advances make larger Lifeless armies possible.

local: about three centuries before the Pahn Kahl rebellion

summary.text: During the Manywar, the two scholars create a sentient sword modeled on a Shardblade.

local: during the Manywar, about three centuries before the Pahn Kahl rebellion

title.text: The Battle of Twilight Falls ends the Manywar

summary.text: The final battle at Twilight Falls closes the conflict; the threat of Kalad’s Lifeless forces helps bring the fighting to an end.
Afterward, Peacegiver establishes Hallandren under the God Kings, while the Idrian royal family remains in exile and forms Idris.

local: about three centuries before the Pahn Kahl rebellion

summary.text: Gemmel trains Kelsier in Allomancy while they investigate a nobleman's search for a new metal.
Kelsier brings Vin into his crew's plan to overthrow the Lord Ruler.

title.text: Kelsier destroys the Pits of Hathsin

summary.text: Kelsier destroys the Pits of Hathsin, cutting off the Lord Ruler's source of atium.
The Lord Ruler kills Kelsier during the uprising, and the skaa take up his cause.
Vin kills the Lord Ruler, ending his rule.
The rebels establish a new government in Luthadel, where Elend is crowned king.
Rival rulers and their armies surround Luthadel, Elend's capital, after the Final Empire's collapse.

title.text: Vin turns the Battle of Luthadel

summary.text: Vin returns to Luthadel and turns the battle, allowing Elend to reclaim the city and rule as emperor.
Vin drains the Well's power, freeing a being that had been imprisoned there.
The being is Ruin, whose escape begins a struggle that threatens Scadrial.
Elend burns a metal bead from the Well and gains Allomantic powers.
Ruin's influence drives worsening ashfall, earthquakes, and Ashmount eruptions across Scadrial.
Elend and his atium-burning soldiers destroy Ruin's atium supply in a last stand against the koloss, and Elend dies with them.

title.text: Sazed takes up the two powers

summary.text: Sazed takes up the powers of Preservation and Ruin as Harmony and begins restoring Scadrial.
The survivors emerge beneath a clear sky onto restored land, ending the ash-covered world.
When the world is remade, the far south turns cold, and the Southern peoples, unable to bear it, die in great numbers in what they call the Ice Death.
After the Catacendre, the Originators, about a fifth of them Terris, found the city of Elendel at the heart of the new Basin.
They are the survivors Harmony sheltered in the storage caverns, and their city bears Elend Venture's name.
The survivors crown Spook emperor and build him a two-storey log house, while Breeze coaches him in ruling and Ham trains him to fight.

title.text: Kelsier and Spook start studying the Metallic Arts

summary.text: Kelsier reaches Spook in a dream, has him wear an Inquisitor spike as an earring so they can talk, and the two agree to study the Metallic Arts and the wider cosmere together.
Breeze, under his true name Edgard Ladrian, founds House Ladrian with Allrianne, who also teaches Elendel's women that they can work as men do while remaining ladies.

title.text: The Sovereign comes to the South

summary.text: About ten years into the Ice Death, a stranger the Southerners call the Sovereign teaches them to make heat medallions, and they take him as king and god.
Memories kept in an old coin suggest the Sovereign was Kelsier, the Survivor.

title.text: The Bands of Mourning hidden in the north

summary.text: The Sovereign carries the Bands of Mourning north with his priests and seals them in a trapped temple in the mountains beyond the Basin, and the priests take the legend home.
After ruling the Basin as emperor for a century, the Lord Mistborn simply disappears, and Elendel stops claiming direct rule over the other cities.
The Lord Mistborn was Spook, made a Mistborn at the Catacendre, whose laws, housing for the poor and Eastern slang shaped Elendel for centuries.

title.text: Siri is sent to marry the God King

summary.text: Siri takes her sister’s place and leaves Idris to become the God King’s bride in Hallandren.

title.text: Lightsong gives his life to save Susebron

summary.text: Lightsong returns his Divine Breath to restore Susebron’s tongue, dying in the act.

title.text: Siri and Susebron stop the Pahn Kahl rebellion

summary.text: After the Pahn Kahl scheme is exposed, Susebron and his allies prevent the Lifeless advance and preserve Hallandren’s rule.
Vasher uses Kalad’s Phantoms to halt the army, and he and Vivenna leave Hallandren together.
Waxillium Ladrian is born into the noble House Ladrian of Elendel.
Wayne is born, and grows up poor with his mother in a mining town.
Steris Harms is born, the daughter of Lord Jackstom Harms.

title.text: Wax kills Forch in the Terris Village

summary.text: At fifteen, during a year in the Terris Village, Wax uncovers the young Twinborn Forch torturing a kidnapped boy and kills him, and the Terris elders' reaction drives him away from the Village.
Marasi Colms is born, Lord Harms's illegitimate daughter and so Steris's younger half-sister.

title.text: Wayne's mother dies in a mine collapse

summary.text: When Wayne is eleven, his mother is killed in a collapse at the mine where she works, leaving him alone.
Wax leaves Elendel's high society for the lawless Roughs, where he teaches himself to be a lawman.
In the Roughs, Wax catches a seventeen-year-old Wayne, who has killed a man in a robbery, spares him, and makes him his deputy.
Hunting the outlaw Granite Joe in Weathering, Wax, with Wayne, teams up with the bounty hunter Lessie, who becomes his partner and later his wife.
Lessie was really the kandra Paalm, whom Harmony had sent to guard Wax, and the romance was her own idea.
After Gavilar's assassination, Elhokar and the Alethi highprinces pledge vengeance, declaring war on the listeners.
During a bridge run, Kaladin realizes that the strength and speed he has shown are Surgebinding.
After her attempt to use the device fails, Shallan admits to Jasnah that she stole it.

title.text: Kaladin turns back at the Tower

summary.text: After Sadeas abandons Dalinar’s force, Kaladin leads Bridge Four back into the battle to help the Kholin soldiers escape.

title.text: Dalinar trades Oathbringer for the bridgemen

summary.text: Dalinar gives Sadeas his Shardblade in exchange for the freedom of the surviving bridgemen.
As the battle at Narak reaches its crisis, the listeners summon the Everstorm while Shallan’s party works to open the Oathgate.
Kaladin intervenes to protect Dalinar and fights Szeth as the Alethi forces are caught in the storm.
The survivors pass through the Oathgate and reach the hidden city, giving the Radiants a base as the Desolation begins.
After Sadeas renews his threat against Dalinar, Adolin kills him in the newly rediscovered city.
Lift swears a new Ideal while protecting the overlooked people of Yeddaw from Nale.

title.text: The truth of the Last Desolation emerges

summary.text: Dalinar, Navani, and Jasnah learn that the final Desolation ended differently from the history they were taught.
Elhokar is killed during the palace assault, and the surviving team escapes the fallen city through the Oathgate into Shadesmar.

title.text: Dalinar rejects Odium and opens a Perpendicularity

summary.text: At Thaylen Field, Dalinar accepts responsibility for his past and opens a Perpendicularity that brings Stormlight to the defenders.

title.text: The Battle of Thaylen Field turns

summary.text: The coalition survives the battle, Odium’s assault is broken, and the survivors begin to rebuild their alliances.

title.text: The sabotage aboard the Wandersail is exposed

summary.text: Rysn uncovers Nikli’s role in the voyage’s escalating dangers as the crew approaches Akinah.

title.text: Rysn agrees to guard the Dawnshard

summary.text: At Akinah, Rysn secures the crew’s safe return by promising to protect the Dawnshard and keep it from falling into the wrong hands.
Raboniel’s forces seize the tower; Navani activates its shield and surrenders, while Kaladin remains at large.
Navani finds the tone that can drive Voidlight from a gemstone, changing what the defenders can do against the Fused.
Maya communicates her choice to the honorspren, challenging their account of the Recreance and the deadeyes.
After accepting that he cannot protect everyone, Kaladin speaks the Fourth Ideal of the Windrunners and hears it accepted in the storm.
Navani establishes a Bondsmith bond with the Sibling, restoring the tower’s defenses and helping free Urithiru.

title.text: The contest of champions is set

summary.text: Dalinar and Odium agree to a contest that will decide the fate of the conflict, with ten days to prepare.
After killing Rayse with Nightblood, Taravangian takes up the Shard of Odium.

title.text: A vision reveals the Recreance’s beginning

summary.text: During the campaign, a vision lets the coalition witness the capture of Ba-Ado-Mishram and the first steps toward the Recreance.
Kaladin tells Nale the story of the Wandersail, helping the Herald reconnect with the people he once tried to protect.
Adolin and the Unoathed hold Azimir's throne room until the contest begins, securing Azir's independence from Odium.
Renarin and Rlain free Ba-Ado-Mishram, repairing the damage her imprisonment caused to Roshar.
Dalinar takes up the Shard Honor.
Taravangian absorbs Honor into Odium, forming Retribution.

title.text: The final day changes the balance of power

summary.text: The confrontation at Urithiru ends with Dalinar and the Stormfather gone, a new Shard in play, and Kaladin bound to a new Oathpact.
In the aftermath, Sigzil accepts Hoid’s Dawnshard and is cast into Shadesmar.

title.text: Wax's uncle and sister reported dead
Edwarn and Telsin fake their deaths

summary.text: Wax's uncle Edwarn and sister Telsin are reported killed in a carriage accident, and House Ladrian calls Wax home from the Roughs to be its High Lord.
Edwarn faked his death; he's Mister Suit, a leader of the secretive Set.
Telsin is alive too, and Edwarn holds her life over Wax.
Hunting the killer Bloody Tan, Wax fires to free the captured Lessie, but Tan pulls her into the shot and she dies; Wax kills Tan.
Lessie was really the kandra Paalm and survived the shot, but with Wax gone back to Elendel her life as Lessie was over.
Back in Elendel as High Lord of House Ladrian, Wax hangs up his guns and spends half a year saving the house's finances.
After Wax and Wayne thwart the Vanishers’ robberies and kidnappings, the Elendel constabulary brings the gang to justice.
Wax stops Bleeder’s attempt to destabilize Elendel and learns her identity as Lessie before she dies.
After unrest and a corruption scandal, Governor Innate is arrested and the Senate later elects Aradel, Elendel’s first governor without noble ancestry.

title.text: The Basin makes contact with the South

summary.text: A Malwish crew’s arrival introduces the Basin to the Southern peoples, and Wax later secures formal contact and an exchange of medallions.

title.text: December sets out to warn the capital

summary.text: After learning of an approaching plague, December leaves home to seek help from the king.
December's party learns that the danger confronting the kingdom has deep historical roots.
December's group enters the palace, but an attempt to control the threat goes badly.

title.text: December helps bring the crisis to an end

summary.text: December's choices help resolve the threat, and the kingdom's leadership changes.

title.text: Elendel asserts authority over the Basin

summary.text: The Senate passes the Elendel Supremacy Bill, granting Elendel authority over the Outer Cities and worsening the political divide.

title.text: The attack on Elendel is stopped

summary.text: Wax and Wayne keep a city-destroying bomb from reaching full strength, though its blast sends a tsunami into Elendel’s docks.
Elendel repeals the Supremacy Bill and the cities establish a National Assembly, bringing the Basin into a shared national government.

title.text: Starling transforms into her dragon form

summary.text: At the age of thirty, Starling undergoes her first transformation into her dragon form.

title.text: Tress sets out to find Charlie

summary.text: After learning Charlie has been taken away, Tress leaves home to attempt a rescue.
A challenge to the ship's command turns violent, leaving Tress and her allies to decide how to respond.

title.text: The crew sails to help Tress

summary.text: When Tress is trapped at the tower, the crew sails in to help her reach the Sorceress.

title.text: Tress breaks the curse and reunites with Charlie

summary.text: Tress identifies how the curse has kept Charlie from her and finds a way to undo it.
Nomad arrives without enough Investiture to understand the people who capture him.
Nomad's attempt to escape with the Beaconites fails, and the group is captured again.
Nomad's plan lets the Beaconites leave their sealed vessels without losing anyone.
The survivors leave Canticle aboard the ship after enduring the planet's dangerous cycle.

title.text: Yumi and Painter's lives become linked

summary.text: Yumi and Painter begin waking in each other's worlds, disrupting their separate routines.

title.text: Yumi and Painter investigate their connection

summary.text: With Design's help, Yumi and Painter examine the unusual connection between them.

title.text: Yumi draws the spirits away from the machine

summary.text: Yumi's towers pull spirits away from the machine and give them a chance to escape.

title.text: Yumi and Painter's story reaches its resolution

summary.text: After the crisis, Yumi and Painter settle into the lives they have chosen.

title.text: Dusk returns to Patji on an expedition

summary.text: Five years before the present-day story, Dusk and Vathi venture into Patji's dangerous night.
Starling's crew finds an island in the Emberdark, where a Scadrian force is already guarding the site they seek.

title.text: The First Company faces a vote of no confidence

summary.text: Vathi waits for the result of a vote that could remove her from the First Company's presidency.
Six months later, Dusk and the officials witness the navigators return from their first excursion.

title.text: Hoid tells the story after Yumi

summary.text: Hoid recounts this story in a later frame narrative set after the events of Yumi.
